questions.prompt: Read: “First Mia mixed the batter. Next, the batter went into the pan. Last, the pan went into the oven.” What happened immediately before the pan went into the oven?
choices: The batter went into the pan.
questions.answer: The batter went into the pan.
questions.explanation: The sequence word “next” marks the step just before the last event.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Read: “The kitten crouched low, wiggled its back legs, and sprang toward the toy mouse.” Which detail best shows the kitten was getting ready to pounce?
choices: It crouched low and wiggled its back legs.
questions.answer: It crouched low and wiggled its back legs.
questions.explanation: Those actions are direct evidence of preparing to pounce.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Read: “Nora tucked the permission slip into the front pocket of the backpack, then checked the pocket twice before leaving.” What can you infer?
choices: Nora thinks the slip is important.
Nora forgot there was a backpack.
Nora wants to lose the slip.
questions.answer: Nora thinks the slip is important.
questions.explanation: Checking the pocket twice shows the slip matters to the character.
